primary_diagnosis_treated: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease with recent myocardial infarction
nice_guideline_used: CG126/NG185 (secondary prevention of IHD) with reference to NG106 for SGLT2‑inhibitor and NG136 for hypertension/CKD considerations

medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 – lifelong low‑dose aspirin for all patients with IHD unless contraindicated

medications.duration: Lifelong – review lipid panel at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce cardiovascular risk and achieve >40 % non‑HDL‑C reduction
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 – high‑intensity statin for all patients with IHD

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily, titrate every 2‑4 weeks to target ≤10 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – renal function and potassium review 1‑2 weeks after each change, then 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Cardioprotective ACE‑I for post‑MI patients, especially with diabetes and CKD
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 & NG136 – ACE‑I recommended for all IHD patients; titrate cautiously in CKD

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily, titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5‑10 mg as tolerated, target HR 55‑60 bpm
medications.duration: Lifelong – monitor heart rate and blood pressure, review after each titration
medications.purpose: Reduce mortality and control angina post‑MI
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 – beta‑blocker first‑line for angina and secondary prevention

medications.duration: Lifelong – renal function and potassium review at baseline, 4 weeks, then 6‑monthly
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular and renal protection in patients with CKD/diabetes (or HFrEF if present)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 / TA902 – SGLT2‑inhibitor recommended for CKD/HF regardless of diabetes, if eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.dose: Start 10 U subcutaneously at night, titrate by 2‑4 U every 3‑4 days to achieve fasting glucose 4.0‑7.0 mmol/L
medications.duration: Lifelong – glucose monitoring daily, review glycaemic control every 2 weeks until stable
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control where metformin is contraindicated by CKD
medications.nice_justification: NICE Diabetes guideline – insulin recommended when oral agents unsuitable in CKD

medications.duration: Lifelong – lipid panel review at 3 months then annually
medications.nice_justification: NICE lipid guideline – consider omega‑3 when triglycerides remain elevated despite statin

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering; risk of symptomatic hypotension, especially during active sepsis
interactions_checked.action: Start both at low doses, monitor BP and symptoms; titrate slowly

interactions_checked.interaction: Both can increase serum potassium; risk of hyperkalaemia in CKD
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K⁺ before initiation and 1‑2 weeks after dose changes; hold if K⁺ >5.5 mmol/L
Educate patient on glucose monitoring; consider modestly lower initial insulin dose

interactions_checked.interaction: Minor increase in statin levels; not clinically relevant with atorvastatin

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 4‑5; NSAIDs worsen renal function and increase CV risk
Negative inotrope; contraindicated in heart failure and may cause bradyarrhythmia with beta‑blocker
contraindications.alternative: Amlodipine if additional calcium‑channel blockade required

contraindications.reason: Negative inotrope; contraindicated in heart failure
Risk of fluid retention and worsening heart failure in CKD
Dual RAAS blockade increases renal injury risk; guideline contraindication
contraindications.alternative: Use ACE‑I alone; switch to ARB only if ACE‑I intolerant

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided; creatinine 3.2 mg/dL approximated to eGFR 20‑30 mL/min/1.73 m². Dapagliflozin only started if calculated eGFR ≥30.
Serum potassium not available; assumed ≤5.0 mmol/L. Must check before ACE‑I and SGLT2‑I initiation.
LVEF not documented; assumed no HFrEF. If LVEF ≤40 %, consider adding MRA and/or ARNI later.
Blood pressure baseline not recorded; titration of ramipril and bisoprolol will depend on measured BP.
Allergy status unknown; must confirm no aspirin, ACE‑I, or statin hypersensitivity before prescribing.
Platelet count 104 ×10³/µL – acceptable for low‑dose aspirin but requires weekly monitoring while sepsis resolves.
Active sepsis noted; hold or reduce beta‑blocker if hypotension develops; reassess once infection controlled.
treatment_summary: The plan initiates guideline‑recommended secondary‑prevention drugs for post‑MI coronary artery disease—low‑dose aspirin, high‑intensity atorvastatin, ramipril, and bisoprolol—while accounting for advanced CKD and active sepsis by using low starting doses and close monitoring. Dapagliflozin is added for CV/renal benefit if eGFR permits, and insulin replaces metformin for glycaemic control. Omega‑3 is offered for residual hypertriglyceridaemia. Contraindicated agents (NSAIDs, verapamil, diltiazem, pioglitazone, ACE‑I + ARB) are avoided. Ongoing labs, vitals, and symptom checks are scheduled per NICE monitoring recommendations.
